rows.name: LSB_HOSTS
rows.values: Host names, separated by whitespace. The runner keeps the part of each name before the first `.`.
rows.default: Unset: the LSF runner uses only the host name of its server, from `socket.gethostname()`.
rows.effect: The LSF runner (the script that an LSF job runs on the FPGA server) treats these names as the names of its server. It checks the requested host and the Dice resource totals against them.
rows.notes: The runner always adds the `socket.gethostname()` name as one more name. The resource totals are the `dice_numa0` and `dice_numa1` counts that `bhosts` reports. A name that does not match `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9.-]*` fails both checks. A failed check stops the job before the work starts.

rows.name: LSB_JOBID
rows.values: Text. TRON does not parse it.
rows.default: Unset: the LSF runner logs `LSF None`. Slice writes no `lsf_job_id` field.
rows.effect: The LSF runner (the script that an LSF job runs on the FPGA server) writes the value into its log. `slice bench` and `slice calibrate` write it into the benchmark lock file as `lsf_job_id`.
rows.notes: The benchmark lock file is `config/.slice-bench.lock`. A Slice process that waits for the lock prints the lock holder with `lsf_job=<value>`. Slice treats an empty value as unset.

rows.name: LSF_ENVDIR
rows.read_by: Nothing in TRON. `bin/dice-lsf-submit`, `bin/dice-lsf-runner` and `bin/dice_lsf_view.py` set it for the LSF commands that they start.
rows.values: Path of the LSF configuration directory. TRON does not parse the text.
rows.default: Unset: the 3 files give their LSF commands `/tools/openlava/etc`. Empty: they keep the empty value.
rows.effect: The 3 files pass it to the LSF commands that they start, for example `bsub`, `bjobs` and `bhosts`. They keep a value from the caller.
rows.notes: The files do not change the environment of their own process. Slice starts its LSF commands through `bin/dice_lsf_view.py`. `bin/bsub-build` (the script that submits a remote build to LSF) starts `bsub` with the caller environment. It adds no default.

rows.name: LSF_SERVER_HOSTS
rows.read_by: Nothing in TRON. `bin/dice-lsf-submit`, `bin/dice-lsf-runner` and `bin/dice_lsf_view.py` remove it for the LSF commands that they start.
rows.values: TRON does not read the value.
rows.effect: The 3 files remove it from the environment of every LSF command that they start. A value from the shell of the user then has no effect on these commands.
rows.notes: A code comment gives the reason: an old shell value can name a retired LSF server. `bin/bsub-build` still passes the value to `bsub`. LSF commands that a user types also get it. `doc/dice.md` says to run those with `env -u LSF_SERVER_HOSTS`.

rows.name: MAKE
rows.values: The command that starts `make`. TRON does not parse it.
rows.default: Unset: GNU Make sets it to the command that started it.
rows.effect: The recipes that start a nested `make` run this command. Examples are the goals `format`, `coverage-report` and `ingest-coverage`.
rows.notes: It is a built-in variable of GNU Make. The makefiles never assign it. GNU Make 4.3 uses a `MAKE` value from the environment in place of its own value.

rows.name: MAKECMDGOALS
rows.values: Make goal names, separated by spaces. Slice removes leading and trailing whitespace.
rows.default: Unset: `make` fills it with the goals of its command line. Slice derives no label from it.
rows.effect: The makefile reads the goals while it parses, for example to refuse `make deb` inside the Nix dev shell. It exports the variable to its recipes. Slice then labels its Dice work `make <goals>`.
rows.notes: For the Slice label, `DICE_LABEL` and `slice submit --label` take priority. GNU Make 4.3 uses a value from its environment in place of the command-line goals. So a nested `make` reads the goals of the outer `make`. `bin/ci/test-make-environment-guidance.sh` unsets the variable for that reason.

rows.name: MAKEFLAGS
rows.values: GNU Make flag text. The makefile looks for a `-jN` word, and for the letters `n`, `q` and `B` in the first word.
rows.default: Unset: GNU Make builds the value from its command-line options.
rows.effect: The makefile appends `--no-print-directory -j $(NPROC_BUILD)`. For a remote build (a build that `bin/bsub-build` submits to an LSF worker), `-jN` sets `REMOTE_BUILD_CORES` to N. The flag `-B` goes to the worker too.
rows.notes: A makefile comment says that GNU Make 4.3 shows `-jN` only inside recipes. There the makefile ignores `-jN` when N equals `NPROC_BUILD`. With `-n` or `-q`, the makefile runs `bin/scratch-dir.sh gen` (the script that creates the build directory) only when `gen` is missing.

rows.name: MAKELEVEL
rows.values: Integer that GNU Make maintains. The makefile compares the text with `0`.
rows.effect: The makefile prints its warning about a run outside the Nix dev shell only when the value is `0`.
rows.notes: The warning also needs empty `IN_NIX_SHELL` and `CI`. GNU Make raises the value by 1 for each nested `make`. `bin/ci/test-make-environment-guidance.sh` removes the variable before it tests the warning. A run with only the goals `deb`, `deb-host` or `gen-deb/...` prints no warning.

evidence.quote: $(warning Running Make outside 'nix develop' is deprecated; this path remains supported during the migration)

rows.name: MAKEOVERRIDES
rows.values: `NAME=value` words. GNU Make fills it with the variable assignments of its command line.
rows.default: Unset: GNU Make fills it from its command line. It is empty when the command line has no assignment.
rows.effect: For a remote build (a build that `bin/bsub-build` submits to an LSF worker), the makefile adds these assignments to the `make` command on the worker. It leaves out `REMOTE`, `REMOTE_HOST`, `REMOTE_MODEL` and `NPROC_BUILD`.
rows.notes: It is a built-in variable of GNU Make. The makefile never assigns it. GNU Make 4.3 uses a value from the environment when the command line has no assignment.

rows.name: MFLAGS
rows.read_by: Nothing in TRON. `bin/ci/test-make-environment-guidance.sh` removes it for 4 `make` commands that it starts.
rows.effect: `bin/ci/test-make-environment-guidance.sh` removes it with `env -u` from the environment of 4 `make` commands. Each of these commands also removes `MAKEFLAGS`, `MAKELEVEL` and `MAKECMDGOALS`.
rows.notes: No file in the repository reads it or gives it a value. The 4 commands test when `make` prints its warning about a run outside the Nix dev shell.

rows.name: NINJA_STATUS
rows.read_by: Nothing in TRON. `nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix` sets it for Ninja.
rows.values: TRON sets the fixed text `[%f/%t elapsed=%es] `. The text ends with one space. Ninja defines the meaning of the `%` codes.
rows.effect: The Nix build `tron-cmake-test-build` sets it for its one `cmake --build` command. Ninja (the build tool that CMake starts) uses it as the format of the progress text that it prints for each build step.
rows.notes: The same command line also sets `TERM=dumb`.

rows.name: NIX_BUILD_CORES
rows.read_by: `ci-select-tron-build-jobs.sh`, `generate.py`, `export.py` and 3 Nix build files (`bin/ci/ci-select-tron-build-jobs.sh`, `bin/ci/model-plugins/generate.py`, `bin/ci/model-traces/export.py` and 3 more files). `nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix` also sets it for `ci-select-tron-build-jobs.sh`.
rows.values: Whole number. `bin/ci/ci-select-tron-build-jobs.sh` accepts digits only and exits with status 2 on other text. `generate.py` and `export.py` parse with `int` and reject values below 1.
rows.default: Unset: 1 job. Empty: the shell code uses 1 job. `export.py` stops with an error. `generate.py` stops with an error when `--jobs` is absent.
rows.effect: Sets the number of parallel jobs in 3 Nix builds: `tron-cmake-test-build` (Ninja jobs), `tron-generated-test-models` (model plugin generation) and `tron-test-model-traces` (model trace export).
rows.notes: With `0`, the shell code uses 1 job. The Ninja build uses at most `NPROC_BUILD` jobs (16 in that build). `generate.py` and `export.py` use at most 16 jobs. `--jobs` replaces the variable. `export.py` still parses the variable and stops on `0` or other bad text.

rows.name: NIX_CFLAGS_COMPILE
rows.values: Compiler option text. The check looks for a word that starts with `-frandom-seed=`.
rows.effect: The flake check `cmake-multi-output-hook-contract` (a check that `nix flake check` runs) passes its build step only when the value holds an option that starts with `-frandom-seed=`.
rows.notes: Without that option the check prints `reproducible-build hook did not set a compiler random seed` and fails. No file in the repository assigns the variable.

evidence.quote: 'reproducible-build hook did not set a compiler random seed' >&2

rows.name: NIX_CONFIG
rows.values: Nix configuration text, one setting on each line. The test does not parse it.
rows.default: Unset: the test starts from empty text.
rows.effect: One test in `bin/ci/nix-cache/test_cache.py` appends 3 settings to the caller value: `trusted-public-keys`, an empty `builders` and `substitute = false`. It passes the result to the workflow steps that it runs with `bash`.
rows.notes: Only test code uses the variable. The steps come from the job `tron-build` of `.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml`.

rows.name: NIX_NO_SELF_RPATH
rows.read_by: Nothing in TRON. `nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix` sets it for the Nix build environment.
rows.values: TRON sets the Nix value `true`.
rows.effect: `nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix` sets it as an attribute of the Nix build `tron-cmake-test-build`. A comment in the file states the purpose: keep the runtime closures of the test output and the benchmark output independent.
rows.notes: A runtime closure is the set of Nix store paths that an output needs at run time. No file in the repository reads the variable. Nix puts the attributes of a build into the environment of its build steps.

evidence.quote: # Keep test and benchmark runtime closures independent.

rows.name: NIX_REMOTE
rows.read_by: Nothing in TRON. `bin/ci/nix-cache/test_cache.py` sets it for the `nix` commands of one test.

rows.name: NO_COLOR
rows.read_by: Nothing in TRON. `bin/ci/test_install_nix_hooks.py` sets it for the commands that the test starts.
rows.values: TRON sets the fixed text `1`.
rows.effect: The test puts `NO_COLOR=1` into the default environment of the commands that it starts: `git`, `bash`, `lefthook` (the Git hook runner) and `bin/install-nix-hooks.py`.

rows.read_by: No TRON code reads the name. Python `urllib` reads it inside `bin/slice`, `bin/hugepage_exhaustion_repro.py` and `bin/ci/hf_cache.py`. The `httpx` library reads it inside `t/proxy/tools/capture.py`. `t/proxy/test_rzproxy.py` removes it.
rows.values: List of hosts that bypass the proxy. TRON code does not parse it.

rows.name: OMP_NUM_THREADS
rows.values: Positive integer. `nproc` prints this number in place of the CPU count.
rows.default: Unset: `nproc` prints the number of CPUs that the process may use.
rows.effect: It changes the default of `NPROC_BUILD` (the number of parallel build jobs). The makefile takes that default from the output of `nproc` and caps it at 16 jobs.
rows.notes: No file in the repository names this variable. The behaviour comes from `nproc` of GNU coreutils. `OMP_THREAD_LIMIT` caps the number that `nproc` prints. No effect when `NPROC_BUILD` already has a value. A value above 16 gives 16 jobs, also on a server with fewer CPUs.

rows.name: OMP_THREAD_LIMIT
rows.values: Positive integer. `nproc` prints at most this number.
rows.default: Unset: `nproc` prints the number of CPUs that the process may use.
rows.effect: It lowers the default of `NPROC_BUILD` (the number of parallel build jobs). The makefile takes that default from the output of `nproc` and caps it at 16 jobs.
rows.notes: A makefile comment says that LSF sets it to the number of reserved cores. No effect when `NPROC_BUILD` already has a value. `bin/bsub-build` defines `NPROC_BUILD` for the `make` of a remote build. `OMP_NUM_THREADS` also changes the output of `nproc`.

evidence.quote: # Cap concurrency to avoid out-of-memory CI hosts. LSF sets OMP_THREAD_LIMIT
# to the reserved cores, and nproc honors it.

rows.name: OSTYPE
rows.values: Text. The scripts test only whether it starts with `darwin`.
rows.default: Unset: bash sets it to the type of its own operating system. On Linux the scripts take the Linux branch.
rows.effect: With a value that starts with `darwin`, the scripts call `stat` and `chmod` in the macOS form. `bin/update-generated-file.sh` then copies only the mode of the file that it replaces.
rows.notes: With any other value, `bin/update-generated-file.sh` copies mode, ownership and extended attributes with `cp`. A value in the environment replaces the value that bash sets. 2 CI test scripts set `OSTYPE=darwin` to run the macOS branch on Linux.

rows.name: PATH
rows.read_by: `dice`, `dice-lsf-runner`, `dice-lsf-submit` and build, CI and test scripts (`bin/dice`, `bin/dice-lsf-runner`, `config/resource-parser.sh` and 39 more files). rinzler and runtron use it without naming it, through `popen` in `src/rinzler/tokenizers.cpp`.
rows.values: List of directories, separated by `:`.
rows.default: Unset: the Dice daemon in shared mode (one daemon for all users) gives a submitted command without `PATH` its own `PATH`, or `/usr/bin:/bin`.
rows.effect: For the Python tokenizer, rinzler and runtron start the script `bin/tokenize_py` through a shell. That script finds `python3` through `PATH`. Several TRON scripts put a tool directory first for the commands that they start.
rows.notes: The LSF runner (`bin/dice-lsf-runner`) puts `/tools/openlava/bin` first for its LSF commands. `config/resource-parser.sh` puts the `bin` directory beside its own directory first when it holds an executable `yq`. The Dice daemon runs `systemctl` and `systemd-run` with `/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin`. `bin/bsub-build` does not pass `PATH` to the remote job.

rows.name: PERFETTO_CONSUMER_SOCK_NAME
rows.values: Path of a Unix socket.
rows.default: Unset: `rinzler-capture.sh` checks `/run/perfetto/traced-consumer.sock` when the directory `/run/perfetto/` exists and is accessible. Otherwise it checks `/tmp/perfetto-consumer`.
rows.effect: `rinzler-capture.sh` (the script that captures a Perfetto trace from a running rinzler) checks this socket before a capture. It stops when a program listens there. It removes an unused socket file that the user owns.
rows.notes: The Perfetto programs that `rinzler-capture.sh` starts inherit the variable. The script stops when another user owns an unused socket file. `bin/ci/perfetto_capture.py` (a capture harness for one command) does not read the variable. It sets `<socket directory>/consumer.sock` for its own Perfetto programs and that command.

rows.name: PS1
rows.read_by: The shell hook of the Nix dev shell (`flake.nix`)
rows.values: Shell prompt text. The hook replaces each `\u` in it.
rows.default: Unset: the hook has no fallback. The prompt becomes `(nix) ` alone.
rows.effect: On x86_64 Linux, the Nix dev shell hook sets the prompt to `(nix) ` plus the old prompt. It replaces each `\u` in the old prompt with the output of `id -un`.
rows.notes: The hook changes the prompt only when `id -un` prints a name. A comment in `flake.nix` calls this a fix for SSSD (the System Security Services Daemon, a login service for directory accounts).

evidence.quote: # 8. PS1 fix for SSSD (must be last to override .bashrc)

new_terms.definition: `bin/dice-lsf-runner`, the script that an LSF job runs on the FPGA server. It starts the work through the Dice daemon of that server.
The script that submits a build command to an LSF worker and shows its output. `make` runs it for build goals when `REMOTE` is `1`, `sku0` or `sku1`.
A build that `make` sends to an LSF worker through `bin/bsub-build`.
A server that LSF gives remote builds and remote test runs to.
The file `config/.slice-bench.lock`. `slice bench` and `slice calibrate` hold a lock on it while they update the benchmarks file.
The Dice mode in which one Dice daemon serves all users of a server.
The Nix build that compiles TRON and its tests with CMake. `nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix` defines it.
The build tool that CMake starts to run the compile steps.
A check that `nix flake check` runs. `flake.nix` defines the checks.
The set of Nix store paths that a Nix build output needs at run time.
The Git hook runner. `lefthook.yml` lists the lint commands that it runs before a commit.
The GNU coreutils command that prints the number of CPUs that a process may use.
The Python tokenizer script. rinzler and runtron run it as a child process when they do not use the Rust tokenizer.
The script `perfetto/tools/rinzler-capture.sh`. It captures a Perfetto trace from a running rinzler.
The System Security Services Daemon, a login service for directory accounts.
The script that creates build directories such as `gen`. It can place them on `/scratch` and link them from the checkout.
A Python module that runs the LSF commands for `bin/slice` and `bin/dice-lsf-submit`. It is not a program.
The capture harness. It starts its own `traced` (the Perfetto daemon) and `perfetto` client around one command and writes a trace file.

notes: All 24 names are kept. No row is dropped. Every evidence quote was found on its cited line. The largest correction is in `NIX_BUILD_CORES`: `bin/ci/model-traces/export.py` stops on the value `0`, although the Nix build file turns `0` into `--jobs 1`. The old row said only that the shell readers turn `0` into 1 job. Facts that no line of the checkout states are marked in the cells with the tool and version that showed them: GNU Make 4.3 for `MAKE`, `MAKECMDGOALS` and `MAKEOVERRIDES`, and `nproc` of GNU coreutils 8.32 for `OMP_NUM_THREADS` and `OMP_THREAD_LIMIT`. They were measured with a scratch makefile and direct commands outside the checkout. GNU Make 4.4, the version of the Nix dev shell, was not measured. The default cells of `MAKE`, `MAKEFLAGS`, `MAKELEVEL` and `MAKEOVERRIDES` describe GNU Make behaviour. `MAKE`, `MAKEOVERRIDES` and `MFLAGS` are built-in variables of GNU Make. The makefiles read `MAKE` and `MAKEOVERRIDES` as make variables, and no TRON code reads them from the process environment. The rows stay under the rule that an environment value of the same name changes the make variable. `OMP_NUM_THREADS`: no file names it. The row rests on `nproc`. `NO_PROXY`: no TRON code reads the name. The read is inside `urllib` and `httpx`. The files in `read_by` are the call sites of those libraries. `PATH`: 42 files name it as a variable. The search covered `$PATH`, `PATH=`, a quoted `PATH`, `export PATH` and `--prefix PATH`. README.md, bin/expert_distribution.py, bin/slice and src/runtron.cpp matched only as option help text or prose and are not counted. Five evidence quotes are a part of their source line: GNUmakefile:96 (three quotes in 2 rows, the line contains the pipe character), GNUmakefile:399 (the line is longer than 120 characters) and flake.nix:1996 (pipe character). The limit of 35 words is applied to every effect cell.
